title: The Path App Versus Care-as-Usual for Moderate Depression and Anxiety
official: A GenAI-Supported Mental Health Platform Versus Care-as-Usual for Moderate Depression and Anxiety
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if The Path, a smartphone app that provides generative AI-supported conversations for emotional support, reduces symptoms of depression and anxiety in U.S. adults experiencing these symptoms.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do participants who use The Path for 8 weeks have greater improvement in depressive and anxiety symptoms than participants receiving care-as-usual?
* Do any improvements last 4 weeks after participants stop using The Path?

Researchers will compare The Path to care-as-usual (the mental health support participants would normally use, or none) to see if The Path reduces depressive and anxiety symptoms.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to use The Path for 8 weeks or continue their usual care
* Complete online surveys at the start of the study and at weeks 4, 8, and 12
* Respond to brief text message check-ins every 2 weeks about any other mental health care they receive
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years; resides within eligible US states
* Able to read and understand English
* Access to smartphone capable of downloading The Path app
* Depressive and/or anxiety symptoms within the study's eligibility range on standardized screening questionnaires
* Able to provide informed consent for participation

Exclusion Criteria:

* Under age 18
* Unable to read or understand English
* Resides outside of the United States or within Nevada, Illinois or Vermont
* Depressive or anxiety symptoms outside the study's eligibility range at screening
* Self-reported diagnoses of severe psychiatric conditions such as schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder with psychotic features, borderline personality disorder, or anorexia nervosa
* Self-reported alcohol or substance abuse or dependency in the past 12 months
* Active suicidal ideation at screening, as determined by screening responses and Study Clinician review
* Does not have access to a smartphone or is unwilling/unable to download the application
* Negative attitude toward AI for mental health
